title: Neuralink Gets FDA Clearance for Pivotal ALS Trial of LINK Implant
summary: Neuralink said it received FDA clearance to start a U.S. pivotal clinical trial, called LINK, of its implanted brain-computer interface in people with ALS. The trial is intended to recruit ALS patients and test direct conversion of brain signals into computer commands; the report describes it as the first U.S. pivotal trial of its kind. Neuralink said more than 30 paralyzed patients have received implants in earlier studies worldwide, and data from the new trial would support a future medical-device marketing application. The report did not provide the trial&\#x27;s size, endpoints, timeline, or independent verification.
